candidate.blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — chest tube dislodgement / emergency management
candidate.educational_objective: Respond to accidental chest-tube removal by immediately occluding the insertion site with sterile petroleum/occlusive dressing and rapidly assessing/escalating respiratory care.

options.A: Immediately cover the insertion site with sterile petroleum-impregnated/occlusive dressing, assess respiratory status, and obtain urgent assistance
options.B: Insert the same chest tube back through the tract at the bedside
options.C: Leave the site open to room air until the provider arrives so pleural air can escape
options.D: Clamp the disconnected drainage tubing and delay assessment until a chest radiograph is obtained

candidate.rationale: NCBI nursing guidance states that when a chest tube dislodges from the patient, the nurse should immediately apply pressure to the insertion site and apply sterile petroleum gauze/occlusive dressing. The client then requires prompt respiratory assessment and urgent clinical assistance because recurrent pneumothorax or respiratory deterioration can occur. The nurse should not reinsert the tube, intentionally leave the thoracic opening uncovered, or postpone assessment. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Accidental chest-tube removal requires immediate occlusion of the thoracic insertion site with sterile petroleum/occlusive dressing and urgent respiratory reassessment/escalation.
